clue.text: Naval musical set round river, Italian one

indicators.note: a thing set round others encloses them, so the show's name wraps the rest

blocks.note: Mame is a Broadway musical
R is the standard abbreviation for river
IT is short for Italian
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A naval-themed stage show is mounted around a river setting with an Italian lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Mame is the 1966 Jerry Herman musical about Auntie Mame; 'set round' makes it the outer shell for the three short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes things connected with the sea and seafaring, as naval matters are.

clue.text: Evil intent shown by male over girl

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man looming over a girl reveals his wicked purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to harm others, which is ill will or evil intent.

clue.text: Forestry official in rage after third of fires

indicators.note: the third of a word means its third letter alone is kept

blocks.note: the third letter
anger is rage

explanation.surface: A forest warden is furious after a series of blazes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In rage' reads as the official's mood, but 'rage' supplies a synonym placed after the selected letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger is a keeper who patrols and manages a forest or park.

clue.text: Airman to let Spit loose

indicators.note: letters let loose are freed from their order and can scatter into a new one

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot is about to release a Spitfire into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Spit is the nickname of the Spitfire, the RAF fighter plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot is an airman who flies new aircraft to check their performance.

clue.text: Very lucrative enterprise producing brass top

blocks.note: brass is British slang for money
a spinning top is a spinner

explanation.surface: A profitable business turning out brass spinning tops.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinner is something that earns a great deal of money.

clue.text: Wine bar round 'East End' of Oslo

indicators.note: on a map east is to the right, so the east end of a word is its tail

blocks.note: taken as written
O is round in shape
the eastern end of the word, read left to right, is its final pair of letters

explanation.surface: Drinking in a pub somewhere in the eastern part of Norway's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' suggests London's Cockney district, but here it just means the right-hand end of Oslo.
explanation.definitionFit: Barolo is a celebrated red wine from Piedmont in north-west Italy.

clue.text: Ballistic missile finally losing tail

indicators.note: losing its tail means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A missile at last loses its tail section.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was an American intercontinental ballistic missile of the Cold War era.

clue.text: Short joke about English passenger ship

blocks.note: on means about, concerning
E is the abbreviation for English
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A quick gag told about an English cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a joke or witty remark delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Excessive action concerning quarry

blocks.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a hunter's kill is the quarry it has brought down

explanation.surface: Going too far in a dispute about a stone pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Overkill is action far beyond what is needed, an excess of force or effort.

clue.text: Cape and bag to despatch

blocks.note: to bag a fish or prize is to land it
to despatch something is to finish it off, to end it

explanation.surface: Instructions to grab a cape and a bag and send them off.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far south-western tip of Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Land's End is a headland, and a cape is a headland projecting into the sea.

clue.text: Charge exorbitantly for wool

blocks.note: first meaning: to overcharge or swindle someone
second meaning: the woolly coat of a sheep

explanation.surface: A trader overpricing the wool they sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece a customer is to rob them through overcharging; a fleece is also the coat of wool shorn from a sheep.

clue.text: Inhalant supplied to order?

blocks.note: surface reading: a medicine made up on request
setter's reading: a religious order of monks, whose members supply the remedy by name

explanation.walkthrough: 'To order' suggests a made-to-order product, but an order is also a body of monks or friars.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar's balsam is a tincture of benzoin added to hot water and inhaled to clear congestion.

clue.text: Fellow importing Ecstasy, low in price

indicators.note: to import is to bring something inside, so one word takes another into its middle

blocks.note: a chap is a fellow
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man smuggling in drugs that sell for very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap costs little money, so it is low in price.

clue.text: Measure criticism after cart overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped end over end, so the word is read backwards
after sends the criticism word to follow the cart word, the reverse of the clue's order

blocks.note: a dray is a heavy cart
to give someone stick is to criticise them

explanation.surface: Assessing the criticism received after a cart has tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: The criticism comes second in the answer because 'after' places it after the cart word.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used for judging or measuring something.

clue.text: The plane flying close up, makes out large sea creature

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered and land in a new order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
to close up a container is to seal it

explanation.surface: From a low-flying aircraft, a passenger spots a large marine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant seal is the largest seal species, a huge marine mammal.

clue.text: Booked acts alternated

blocks.note: to take a room or seat is to book it
turns are variety acts on stage

explanation.surface: The music-hall acts that were booked appeared one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: People who took turns did something in alternation, one after the other.

clue.text: Rays seen here in Florida?

blocks.note: surface reading: a sunny spot or a place to watch stingrays
setter's reading: the Rays are a Major League Baseball team named after the place

explanation.walkthrough: Rays suggests sunshine or fish, but it is the baseball team based on Florida's Gulf coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa Bay is the home of the Rays baseball club and an inlet where rays swim.

clue.text: Delicacy got from fair goes off

indicators.note: something that goes off explodes or spoils, so its letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fancy food bought at a fair that turns rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Foie gras, fattened goose or duck liver, is a luxury food item.

clue.text: Feasts, at noon, prepared quite frequently

indicators.note: food prepared is worked into a new form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lunchtime banquets are laid on regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As often as not' is an idiom meaning about half the time, so fairly frequently.

clue.text: Ammo is moved about in sensitive plant

indicators.note: things moved about are shifted out of place, so the letters change order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ammunition is shifted around inside a delicate plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa pudica is called the sensitive plant because its leaves fold up when touched.

clue.text: Cocksure supporters, extremely stroppy

indicators.note: at the extremes of a word are its first and last letters only

blocks.note: bras are supporting garments
the outer letters

explanation.surface: Arrogant fans who are also very bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy means bold and brazen, showing an overconfident, cocky manner.

clue.text: Remarkable things - father describes small number collected by macho types

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw a line around, so the parent word encloses the rest
something collected by people is gathered in among them, so it sits inside

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
he-men are macho men
No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A dad tells of the odd sights a small group of tough men gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the abbreviation sits inside the macho men, and father wraps around the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena can mean extraordinary events or people, things regarded as remarkable.

clue.text: Honours European, extremely fat

blocks.note: OBEs are British honours, Officers of the Order of the British Empire
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A very fat European is showered with awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes someone grossly overweight, which is very fat.

clue.text: German city judge?

blocks.note: first meaning: an ancient city on the Moselle
second meaning: one who tries cases, a whimsical noun from the verb

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'one who tries' is a playful coinage rather than a dictionary sense of judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is a Roman-founded city in western Germany; a judge tries cases, so is jokingly a trier.

clue.text: A hardy grass from an Indonesian island, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

blocks.note: Bali is an island of Indonesia

explanation.surface: A tough grass is said to come from Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where the R in the grain is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley is a cereal crop, botanically a hardy member of the grass family.

clue.text: Taking a great deal of interest?

definitions.text: Taking a great deal of interest?

blocks.clueFragment: Taking a great deal of interest?
blocks.note: surface reading: being very curious or engaged in something
setter's reading: interest as money charged on a loan, taken in excessive amounts

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fascination; the financial sense of interest gives the moneylender's vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurious lending charges extortionate rates, so the lender takes a great deal of interest money.

clue.text: They always agree sheikh's head in Red Sea republic

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so we keep only the opening letter
placed in a country's name means it sits inside that word

blocks.note: Yemen borders the Red Sea
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A sheikh's chief is placed in a Middle Eastern state among compliant courtiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheikh's head' looks like a ruler, but it is just the first letter of sheikh.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who agree with everything their superior says.

clue.text: Envoy has girl in the course of disrupted

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged
placing one thing in another puts it inside that word

blocks.note: read here as a stretch of time, a year; the clue as published seems to have lost the word year itself
miss is a title for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: An envoy brings a young woman along during a chaotic period.
explanation.walkthrough: The published clue looks truncated: it almost certainly ended 'in the course of disrupted year'. As printed, the only source for the jumbled four letters is 'the course of' read as a span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a person sent on a mission as a representative, the same as an envoy.
